answer: Because the timber forfeiture is applied at exit, the nectar ledger totals each burn, and the hollow audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 22 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 60% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and therefore nobody profits from it. That is 31 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
